q: A company wants to block hateful, violent, and sexual content in both user prompts and model responses for its Amazon Bedrock chatbot, with configurable strength. Which feature fits?
options: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput with a commitment
notes: Correct. Guardrails content filters detect harmful categories (such as hate, insults, sexual content, violence, and misconduct) in inputs and outputs, with adjustable filter strength.
Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity; it does not filter content.
Object Lock prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten.
Cost Explorer analyzes spending.
explain: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is the main responsible AI tool named in skill 4.1.2. One guardrail can combine content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive information filters, and contextual grounding checks.

q: A bank's customer assistant must never give personalized investment advice, even if users ask indirectly. Which Amazon Bedrock Guardrails policy is designed for this?
options: Model distillation for a smaller assistant
notes: Correct. Denied topics let you describe subjects the application must avoid; matching prompts or responses are blocked with a custom message.
Grounding checks catch answers unsupported by source content, not off-limits topics.
Prompt caching is a cost feature.
Distillation creates a smaller model and does not restrict topics.
explain: Denied topics are defined in natural language with a description and example phrases, so the guardrail can catch indirect requests too, not just exact keywords.
ref: Exam guide skill 4.1.2; Bedrock Guardrails denied topics

q: A healthcare chatbot must not repeat phone numbers, email addresses, or ID numbers in its responses. Which Guardrails feature handles this?
options: Sensitive information filters that block or mask PII
Increasing the model's maximum output tokens for every response
notes: Correct. Sensitive information filters detect PII types (and custom regex patterns) and can block the content or mask it in responses.
Profanity word filters do not detect personal data formats.
Denied topics block subjects, not data patterns such as phone numbers.
Output length has nothing to do with PII.
explain: Guardrails sensitive information filters help prevent data leakage. Amazon Macie (for data in S3) and Amazon Comprehend (PII detection in text) are related tools.
ref: Exam guide skills 4.1.2 and 5.1.4 (data leakage prevention)

q: A retailer's assistant must never mention specific competitor brand names or certain offensive words. Which Guardrails policy is simplest for this?
notes: Correct. Word filters block exact words and phrases you list, plus a managed profanity list.
Grounding checks compare answers with source material.
PII filters detect personal data patterns, not brand names.
Evaluation jobs measure quality; they do not block words at run time.
explain: Choose the guardrail policy that fits the problem: word filters for exact terms, denied topics for subjects, content filters for harmful categories, and PII filters for personal data.

q: Which statement about Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is correct?
options: Guardrails check both inputs and outputs, and can also protect models outside Bedrock via the ApplyGuardrail API
Guardrails can only inspect the responses a model generates; they never look at what users type into the application
Guardrails work only with one specific model family on Bedrock and must be rebuilt for every other model
Guardrails permanently retrain the foundation model to remove harmful knowledge from its weights
notes: Correct. Guardrails check prompts and responses, and the ApplyGuardrail API lets you use the same policies with any model or application.
Guardrails inspect inputs as well, for example to catch prompt attacks.
Guardrails are model-agnostic.
Guardrails filter at run time; they do not change model weights.
explain: Because guardrails sit outside the model, one consistent safety policy can cover many models and applications.
ref: Exam guide skill 4.1.2; Bedrock Guardrails ApplyGuardrail

q: Match each Amazon Bedrock Guardrails policy to the problem it solves.
prompts: Block hate, violence, and sexual content
Stop the assistant from discussing legal advice
Mask customers' phone numbers and email addresses
Block a list of exact banned terms
Catch answers not supported by the retrieved source documents
explain: Guardrails policies can be combined in one guardrail and applied to inputs, outputs, or both. Automated reasoning checks are a further policy that verifies responses against formal rules.

q: A hiring model recommends male candidates more often than equally qualified female candidates. Which responsible AI dimension is most clearly violated?
notes: Correct. Treating equally qualified groups differently is a fairness and bias problem.
Robustness is about reliable behavior under unexpected inputs.
Latency is about speed, not a responsible AI dimension.
Veracity is about truthfulness of outputs.
explain: Responsible AI features listed in skill 4.1.1 include bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, and veracity. Bias in hiring can also create legal risk.

q: A model works well on clean test data but behaves unpredictably when users type with spelling mistakes or unusual phrasing. Which responsible AI dimension needs improvement?
notes: Correct. Robustness means performing reliably when inputs are noisy, unexpected, or adversarial.
The issue described is reliability under noisy input, not who is represented in data.
Transparency is about explaining how the system works.
Sustainability concerns environmental impact.
explain: Improve robustness with varied and noisy training data, adversarial testing, input validation, and guardrails.

q: Which responsible AI dimension is most concerned with whether a model's outputs are truthful and accurate?
notes: Correct. Veracity means the system produces correct, truthful outputs.
Inclusivity concerns serving diverse users well.
Sustainability concerns environmental impact.
Tone control is a style concern.
explain: Hallucinations directly threaten veracity. Grounding with RAG, contextual grounding checks, and human review support it.

q: A voice assistant understands some accents far better than others, so many customers cannot use it reliably. Which responsible AI feature is lacking?
notes: Correct. Inclusive AI works well for the full range of people who use it, including different accents, languages, and abilities.
Prompt caching is a cost optimization.
Provisioned Throughput is a capacity option.
Speed does not fix poor understanding of accents.
explain: Inclusivity starts with diverse, representative training and test data, plus testing results for each user group.

q: Which actions support the safety dimension of responsible AI for a public chatbot? Select TWO.
options: Filter harmful content in inputs and outputs with guardrails
Red-team the system with adversarial prompts before launch
Disable all logging to save storage costs
Raise the temperature to make answers more varied
Remove human escalation paths to reduce costs
notes: Correct. Guardrails reduce the chance of harmful outputs.
Correct. Adversarial testing (red teaming) finds safety gaps before users do.
Logs are needed to detect and investigate safety incidents.
More randomness can increase unsafe or off-topic outputs.
Human escalation is an important safety net.
explain: Safety means preventing harmful outputs and misuse. It combines guardrails, testing, monitoring, and human oversight.

q: A company wants to reduce the environmental impact of its GenAI solution while keeping quality acceptable. Which choice helps most?
options: Use the smallest model that meets the need, and reuse pretrained models rather than training from scratch
Always choose the largest and newest model available, for every task, so quality is never at risk
Retrain a brand-new foundation model from scratch every month so it always has the latest knowledge
Run every request several times on different models, then keep whichever answer looks best
notes: Correct. Smaller models and reuse of existing models need far less energy for training and inference.
The largest models use the most compute per request.
Repeated pretraining consumes huge amounts of energy.
Running requests several times multiplies compute and energy use.
explain: Responsible model selection includes environmental impact and sustainability (skill 4.1.3). Efficient hardware such as AWS Inferentia and AWS Trainium, and right-sized models, also help.

q: A marketing team publishes an AI-generated image that closely resembles a famous copyrighted illustration. What legal risk does this create?
options: Data residency violation in the EU Region
Higher token prices on future requests
notes: Correct. Generated content that copies protected work can lead to IP infringement claims.
Data residency concerns where data is stored or processed.
Underfitting is a model training problem, not a legal risk.
Token prices are unrelated to legal exposure.
explain: GenAI legal risks in skill 4.1.4 include IP infringement claims, biased outputs, loss of customer trust, end-user risk, and hallucinations. Mitigate with review processes, provenance tracking, and content policies.

q: A telecom's chatbot gives a customer confidently wrong information about contract cancellation fees, and the story spreads on social media. Which risks does this mainly illustrate?
options: Hallucination leading to loss of customer trust
Overprovisioned throughput leading to higher cost
Model drift caused by a new instance type
Poor chunk overlap leading to slower retrieval
notes: Correct. An invented answer (hallucination) damages trust and can create legal and financial exposure.
Throughput settings do not cause wrong answers.
Instance types do not cause drift or wrong policy answers.
Chunk overlap affects retrieval quality, not the reputational impact described.
explain: Hallucinations are listed as a legal and business risk. Ground answers in official documents, cite sources, and route policy questions to verified content or people.
ref: Exam guide skill 4.1.4 (loss of customer trust, hallucinations)

q: A wellness app's AI assistant suggests a dangerous dosage to a user who asks about medication. Which GenAI risk category does this best represent?
notes: Correct. Harm to the people using the system is end-user risk.
Data lineage concerns tracking where data came from.
Distillation is a training technique, not a risk category.
Prompt caching does not cause harmful advice.
explain: High-risk domains such as health, finance, and law need strict guardrails (for example, denied topics), clear disclaimers, and escalation to qualified humans.

q: Which are legal or business risks of using generative AI? Select TWO.
options: Biased outputs that harm certain groups
notes: Correct. Generated content may infringe others' IP.
Correct. Biased outputs can lead to discrimination claims and reputational damage.
Lower cost is a benefit, not a risk.
Speed to market is a benefit.
Model size is a design choice, not a legal risk.
explain: The full list in skill 4.1.4 is IP infringement claims, biased model outputs, loss of customer trust, end-user risk, and hallucinations.

q: A face-verification model was trained mostly on photos of people with lighter skin, and it has much higher error rates for people with darker skin. Which dataset problem caused this?
options: The dataset was not diverse or balanced across groups
The dataset was stored in too many S3 buckets
The images were too high in resolution
The model was trained for too many epochs on the same photos
notes: Correct. Under-represented groups get worse performance when training data lacks diversity and balance.
Storage layout has no effect on model fairness.
High resolution does not cause group-specific errors.
Epoch count does not explain a systematic gap between groups.
explain: Skill 4.1.5 lists inclusivity, diversity, curated data sources, and balanced datasets as important characteristics. Measure performance per subgroup to detect such gaps.

q: A team is building a dataset to fine-tune a medical Q&A model. Which source choice best supports responsible AI?
options: Curated, vetted sources such as peer-reviewed material and approved clinical guidelines
Any medical-sounding text scraped from random online forums and comment threads
Only marketing pages published by supplement sellers and wellness brands
Synthetic answers generated by another model and used without any human review
notes: Correct. Curated, trustworthy sources improve accuracy and reduce harmful misinformation.
Unvetted forum text can contain dangerous misinformation.
Marketing pages are biased and often inaccurate.
Unreviewed synthetic data can spread errors.
explain: Curated data sources are listed in skill 4.1.5. In high-stakes domains, data provenance and expert review are essential.

q: A model scores 98% on training data and 70% on test data. In bias-variance terms, what is happening?
options: Low bias and low variance (an ideal fit)
notes: Correct. High variance means the model is too sensitive to the training data and does not generalize.
High bias shows as poor performance on training data too.
An ideal fit would perform well on both datasets.
Poisoning is malicious data tampering, which nothing in the scenario suggests.
explain: Bias-variance trade-off: high bias leads to underfitting (too simple), and high variance leads to overfitting (too complex). Both cause inaccuracy, and both can affect demographic groups unevenly.
ref: Exam guide skill 4.1.6 (bias and variance, overfitting, underfitting)

q: A model performs poorly on both training and test data. What is the most likely issue, and one way to address it?
options: Underfitting; use a more capable model or better features
Overfitting; add more regularization and stop training earlier
Data leakage; delete the test set and evaluate on training data
Model drift; lower the temperature and redeploy the same model
notes: Correct. Poor results everywhere suggest the model is too simple or lacks informative features (high bias).
Regularization reduces overfitting and would make underfitting worse.
Deleting the test set removes the ability to measure anything.
Temperature applies to generative sampling, not to this training problem.
explain: Underfitting fixes: more expressive models, better feature engineering, more training time, and less regularization.

q: A loan model's overall accuracy is 92%, but the team suspects it is less accurate for applicants over 60. What should it do to check?
options: Run a subgroup analysis comparing metrics across age groups
Look only at the overall 92% accuracy figure, since it is already high
Increase the size of the model
Train for more epochs and check overall accuracy again
notes: Correct. Subgroup analysis breaks metrics down by group to reveal hidden performance gaps.
Overall accuracy can hide poor performance for a minority group.
A bigger model does not show whether a gap exists.
Overall accuracy again hides the subgroup issue.
explain: Tools and methods in skill 4.1.7 include label quality analysis, human audits, and subgroup analysis. SageMaker Clarify computes bias metrics across groups.

q: Which AWS tool can measure bias in a dataset before training (for example, class imbalance between groups) and in a trained model's predictions?
notes: Correct. SageMaker Clarify computes pre-training and post-training bias metrics and also explains predictions with feature attributions.
Polly converts text to speech.
Secrets Manager stores credentials.
CloudFront delivers content.
explain: Clarify supports fairness (bias detection) and explainability (feature importance with SHAP). It can also be used with model monitoring to detect bias drift in production.

q: While reviewing a sentiment dataset, a team finds that different annotators labeled the same reviews very differently. What should it investigate?
options: Label quality, for example agreement between annotators and clarity of the labeling guidelines
The model's maximum output tokens and its temperature setting during inference
The number of AWS Regions in which the labeling data is currently stored
The index type and the distance metric used by the knowledge base's vector store
notes: Correct. Inconsistent labels teach the model noise and can embed annotators' biases; label quality analysis finds and fixes this.
Output length is unrelated to labeling.
Region count does not affect label quality.
Vector indexing is unrelated to supervised labels.
explain: Label quality analysis is one of the methods listed in skill 4.1.7. Clear guidelines, annotator training, and consensus labeling (supported in SageMaker Ground Truth) improve it.

q: A company has independent reviewers regularly examine a sample of its AI system's decisions for fairness and correctness. What is this practice called?
notes: Correct. Human audits review real outputs to catch bias, errors, and trust issues that metrics may miss.
Prompt caching is a cost feature.
Batch transform is an offline inference method.
Chunking splits documents for retrieval.
explain: Human audits complement automated metrics. They are listed in skill 4.1.7 as a way to monitor bias, trustworthiness, and truthfulness.

q: A credit model passed fairness checks at launch. The team wants to be alerted if its predictions become biased over time as the applicant population changes. What should it set up?
options: Ongoing bias drift monitoring in production, for example SageMaker Model Monitor with Clarify bias metrics
A one-time bias report generated at launch and archived in Amazon S3 Glacier for audits
A higher temperature setting for the credit model so its predictions vary more over time
A new prompt template for the credit model's inputs, reviewed by the compliance team once
notes: Correct. Monitoring bias metrics on live predictions detects drift so the team can retrain or adjust.
A one-time report cannot detect later changes.
Temperature does not apply to this kind of model or problem.
Prompt templates do not monitor bias.
explain: Fairness is not one-and-done. Monitor deployed models for data, quality, and bias drift, and act on alerts.

q: Match each responsible AI dimension to the scenario that most clearly tests it.
prompts: A model gives equal outcomes to equally qualified applicants from all groups
A model keeps working correctly when inputs contain typos or odd phrasing
A model's statements are true and accurate
A speech model works well for users with many different accents
explain: Skill 4.1.1 lists bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, and veracity as features of responsible AI systems.
